name: TECfusions, Inc. (Florida corporation, document P23000017138; site entities include Tecfusions Keystone LLC and TECfusions Clarksville LLC)
headquarters: Clearwater, Florida, USA (19995 US Highway 19 N); earlier releases datelined Tampa; the Florida registry lists a Gulfport, FL principal address
employees: Not disclosed; the LinkedIn company page shows the 51–200 band (55 listed)

ownership.notes: Privately held, 100% by the founder: the Stockholder Support Agreement of 21 Jul 2026 (SEC exhibit) names 'Jeremiah 29:11, LLC', whose sole member is the Simon Tusha Revocable Trust dated 28 May 2025, as holder of '100% of the Company common stock'. A Business Combination Agreement signed 21 Jul 2026 with Apex Treasury Corporation (Nasdaq: APXT, a Cayman SPAC with about US$353M in trust at 30 Jun 2026) values TECfusions at US$4.0 billion pre-money (400.0 million new shares at US$10.00), with a US$35M PIPE from Eleven Ventures LLC, an expected Nasdaq ticker of 'TECF', a targeted close in Q4 2026 and an outside date of 31 Mar 2027. It is signed, not closed: no Form S-4 had been filed on EDGAR as of 29 Sep 2026. Pro forma ownership: TECfusions holders 89.0%, SPAC public 7.6%, sponsor 2.6%, PIPE 0.8%. The founder may sell up to US$100 million inside the six-month lock-up. The investor deck's risk factors state that results 'may be adversely affected by its founder's and majority shareholder's prior criminal convictions and alleged misconduct'.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: TECfusions is a founder-owned Florida developer that leases 'space, power, and cooling' in re-used industrial buildings, is TensorWave's landlord in Tucson and Pennsylvania, and is the only landlord in this corpus that says its flagship campus is 'currently powered by turbines' it controls. Its record is small next to its claims: 37 MW live at Clarksville, Virginia, 16 MW at Tucson (a building it rents) and 2 MW at Keystone Connect against a marketed '3 GW' for that site, a '1 GW' TensorWave figure that the company's own deck calls 'anchor tenant with right-of-first-refusal', and a US$4.0 billion SPAC valuation that is signed but not closed. BACKGROUND: Founded in February 2023 by Simon Tusha, a former Google negotiator who served 21 months in federal prison for an IRS conspiracy tied to kickbacks; the company discloses the convictions as a risk factor. It built Clarksville's first halls in months in 2024 under a US$300 million-plus loan from an unnamed 'dedicated investor', took a 15-year net lease on a former NortonLifeLock data centre in Tucson, and bought 1,395 acres of the former Alcoa research campus in Upper Burrell, Pennsylvania in December 2024 (not Clarion, and not a glass plant, as the coverage-plan row had it). Keystone Connect went live in Building J in mid-2026 with 2 MW leased and 10 MW contracted, environmental permits held by Tecfusions Keystone LLC, no located air permit, and a township moratorium, a draft 'bring your own baseload' ordinance and a residents' land-use appeal around it. Business-combination projections run revenue from US$110M in 2026 to US$2.14B in 2028 with US$34 billion of debt-funded capex; the financials are unaudited. Per company documents and the SEC filings of its SPAC counterparty unless stated; EDGAR was reachable from this session.
ecosystemRole: We assess TECfusions as a challenger in the AIDC developer and landlord segment and an adjacent member of the bridge and on-site generation segment: it is a landlord that is also, by its own account, the generator. Basis: its deck says 'Design, build and lease AI-ready data centers', 'Avoid providing the volatile, expensive and high-risk GPU/compute capacity layer' and 'Operate a real estate landlord / developer business model with long-term contracted lease revenues'; its services pages sell 'reliable power through our self generated natural gas systems'; its August 2026 release says New Kensington is 'currently powered by turbines' and will move to 'dual utility and on-site microgrid generation' on 'two fracking pads and a gas-drying plant'. It signs for the whole chain it builds: the founder says 'we use continuous duty-rated equipment', the RACP grant scope lists 'generation, UPS, switchgear, cabling', and its supply-chain blog names transformers ('up to four years for medium and high voltage units'), switchgear (12 to 18 months), chillers, generators and UPS as the items it buys around. No turbine OEM, switchgear vendor, EPC, gas supplier or utility is named anywhere on the record, no battery, SST or 800 VDC project exists, and one local report says Building J still draws grid power. For a power-equipment seller the buying authority is real and unusually direct, and the counterparty risk is equally direct: a single owner, one anchor tenant, unaudited financials and a pending SPAC.

productsAndServices.name: Leased AI-ready data-centre capacity — shell, colocation and turnkey
productsAndServices.description: TECfusions builds and leases high-density halls in re-used industrial buildings and sells 'Shell, colocation and turnkey options for hyperscalers and neoclouds' (deck). Its services pages offer Colocation ('a single rack, a private suite, or a customized cage' with a 99.999% SLA), HyperScale ('vast amounts of space' on 'self-generated natural gas systems') and AI/HPC hosting with liquid and air cooling. Pricing is 'based on the quantum of power per client at a fixed price per kW, with annual escalators and subject to multi-year contractual obligations'; the CEO said 'our shortest remaining term is 12 years, maybe 13 years'. Sites: Clarksville, VA (37 MW live and fully leased, 42 MW under contract in a 220 MW Phase 2, 300 MW target on 73 added acres); Tucson, AZ (16 MW live, 12 MW contracted, a 20 MW Phase 2 on the Arizona grid); Keystone Connect, Upper Burrell, PA (2 MW live, 10 MW contracted, 'up to 3 GW' planned by 2031).
highlights: TensorWave is the only tenant the company names: a 'landmark 1 GW capacity commitment' (31 Oct 2024) that the deck restates as '1 GW anchor tenant with right-of-first-refusal'; 14.4 MW delivered at Tucson in 2025 'in under 4 months'; 20 MW added in Jan 2026, split 10 MW Tucson and a 10 MW first phase at Keystone Connect on AMD MI300X, MI325X and MI355X; TribLive later reported the Building J tenant as 'Undisclosed due to non-disclosure agreement. Previously reported as TensorWave'
Speed as the product: 'Contract to deployment in less than 6 months' on every flyer; Clarksville's 10.5 MW C-Hall was built 'in 3 months' (Sep 2024)
Capex 'US$10 to 13 million per megawatt' for contracted capacity excluding the Pennsylvania power plant; 'We develop largely to order' (CFO-designate, Jul 2026 webinar)
Deck projections (unaudited): MW in service 92 (2026), 422 (2027), 1,467 (2028); a '675+ MW potential tenant pipeline' of contracts 'which may be executed within the next 2 years'
productsAndServices.positioning: The deck's 2×2 places traditional developers as 'Slow + Grid-Dependent, 12-24 mo. build cycles', behind-the-meter power-as-a-service as 'Fast + Power-Only', and TECfusions as 'Fast + Vertically Integrated, <6 mo. deployment | On-site power'. No competitor is named. In this corpus the nearest models are Fermi America (generation-first campus, also a TensorWave landlord) and the converted miners; TECfusions is smaller than any of them in energised capacity.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term leases priced per kW with escalators (12- to 15-year terms); master service agreements with the anchor neocloud
targetSegments: hyperscalers and enterprise AI users (company targets)
sovereign and public-sector users (a 40 MW Uganda MOU, 2023; Chile with Baeza Group)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Clarksville Phase 2 capacity 'Q3 of 2026'; Tucson Phase 2 20 MW 'energizing'; Keystone Phase 1 '300 MW' in 18 to 24 months and 1.1 GW IT, 3 GW by 2031; Puente Alto, Chile 10 MW rising to 100 MW; sites 'identified' in Norway (all company statements)

productsAndServices.name: On-site natural-gas generation and microgrids — 'TECfusions Power Control'
productsAndServices.description: The company's stated point of difference: it generates its own power. Keystone Connect is 'Currently powered by turbines', with a 'future power plan' of 'dual utility and on-site microgrid generation, supported by existing site infrastructure, including two fracking pads and a gas-drying plant' and 'on-site wells accessing Marcellus Shale natural gas' (Aug 2026 release; SEC 425). The deck aims at '99.999% uptime via on-site natural gas-fired microgrids with layered redundancy', 'Low-emission turbines supporting Pennsylvania clean energy goals', and a New Kensington power plant 'operating from Q4 '27 onwards' that contributes 'approximately $0.5B in revenue during 2028'. Blogs price gas power 'as low as 4 cents per kWh' under 15-year agreements and 'under 5 cents per kWh' for hyperscalers, and say turbine waste heat is repurposed 'to lower the PUE'. Clarksville's site plan includes 'a microgrid'; Tucson has 'dual utility and on-site power for 15 MW critical power'.
highlights: No turbine OEM, model, unit size or count is named in any company or third-party document; the Environmental Integrity Project models a 'TECfusions Keystone Connect Power Plant' of 2,700 MW from the announced capacity, 'New — 2031/Unknown'

No Pennsylvania DEP air-quality plan approval, general permit or Title V in TECfusions' name was found in the PA Bulletin; the permits located are NPDES PA0000469 and two water-quality permits transferred to Tecfusions Keystone LLC in March and April 2025

Conflict on the record: the company says Building J is 'powered by turbines'; TribLive (28 Aug 2026) says it is 'currently drawing from existing grid power lines; transitioning to onsite natural gas generation'. Gas ownership is also unconfirmed: the company says wells it owns, while Allegheny Front photographed EQT signage at wells by the site

Equipment philosophy: 'we use continuous duty-rated equipment … We're not doing emergency or standby equipment' (founder, Jul 2026 webinar); the deck names 'domestic sourcing of Transformers, HVAC, immersion cooling'
productsAndServices.positioning: Against the corpus's bridge-power vendors (VoltaGrid, Enchanted Rock, ProEnergy), TECfusions is a buyer and owner of generation rather than a seller of it; against Fermi America it is far earlier: 2 MW live and no permit trail, where Fermi has 1.5 GW of turbines landed.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled into the lease as a power price per kWh under 15-year terms
productsAndServices.roadmap: New Kensington power plant from Q4 2027 (deck); 'Operating 100% off-grid when needed' (sustainability page); a township draft ordinance would require every new data centre to 'supply its own baseload power'

productsAndServices.name: Adaptive-reuse site development
productsAndServices.description: The company's method is to buy or lease legacy industrial and corporate sites with existing power infrastructure and convert them: the former Alcoa/Arconic Technical Center at Upper Burrell (1,395 acres, 'more than one million square feet' of structures, closed 2 Dec 2024, price undisclosed, a US$2M state RACP grant); Clarksville's 22.5-acre site plus 73 acres bought in Feb 2025 with a plan to 'repurpose abandoned 138kV transmission lines from a decommissioned coal plant' in discussion with Dominion Energy and Mecklenburg County; and Tucson's 1989 data centre, leased from Aphorio Carter Fund Management on a 15-year absolute triple-net lease after the landlord bought it for US$13M in October 2023.
highlights: Keystone Connect's approvals: a building permit in 2025 with 'zoning permits deemed unnecessary'; a Building J land-development plan approved 5 Aug 2026 ('generator and chiller replacement'); Phase 2 approval tabled in June 2026; a 180-day township moratorium (to 2 Nov 2026) with TECfusions 'grandfathered in'; a residents' land-use appeal filed 25 Aug 2026 in Westmoreland County court
A US$300 million-plus, 15-year loan for Clarksville Phase I from an unnamed 'dedicated investor' (Oct 2024), with US$160M allocated to construction
Puente Alto, Chile: a 40-acre site with Baeza Group, 10 MW initial and 100 MW planned (Jun 2025); a 2023 Uganda MOU; a 'Lista, Norway site identified' (Mar 2025)
productsAndServices.positioning: The same retrofit thesis as WhiteFiber's Enovum in this corpus, at earlier stage and with the company itself as the generator.
targetSegments: legacy industrial sites with gas and grid access
productsAndServices.roadmap: Keystone Phases 2–5 to 2031; Chile 100 MW; no dates for Norway

relationships.via: TensorWave as the shared anchor tenant
relationships.note: Fermi America signed a 222 MW, 15-year lease with TensorWave TEX1, LLC on 9 Aug 2026; TECfusions holds TensorWave's earlier '1 GW' commitment and its Tucson and Keystone Connect phases, so the two landlords now compete for the same tenant's growth.
relationships.context: TensorWave's June 2026 Series B announcement claims 'over 2 gigawatts of long-term capacity secured' and names neither landlord. Fermi's lease is binding but conditional on project financing and a guarantor by 30 Sep 2026 (per the corpus's Fermi dossier); TECfusions' commitment is described in its own deck as 'anchor tenant with right-of-first-refusal'. Both are generation-first developers; Fermi has 1.5 GW of turbines landed and TECfusions 2 MW live.

relationships.via: Dominion Energy Virginia service at Clarksville; 138 kV line reuse under discussion
relationships.note: Clarksville takes grid service from Dominion Energy Virginia (the site is listed as operational under Dominion by interconnection.fyi), and TECfusions' February 2025 release describes discussions with Dominion and Mecklenburg County to repurpose abandoned 138 kV lines from a decommissioned coal plant.
relationships.context: Dominion has issued no statement naming TECfusions on the record; the relationship is recorded from TECfusions' release and an aggregator's interconnection listing. The 300 MW Clarksville target depends on that line reuse, which the company describes as 'under discussion'.

policyExposure.regime: Upper Burrell Township data-centre moratorium and draft ordinance
policyExposure.exposure: A 180-day moratorium adopted in May 2026 runs to 2 Nov 2026 with TECfusions' existing permits grandfathered. The revised draft ordinance (Aug 2026) would require every new data centre to supply its own baseload power, impose 500- and 1,000-foot setbacks and a 75 dB limit; the planning commission paused it on 22 Sep 2026 ahead of a 7 Oct supervisors' meeting. The township has no ordinance regulating power plants. Phases 2 to 5 of Keystone Connect would be permitted under whatever is adopted.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company says the project is 'aligned with' Governor Shapiro's Executive Order 2026-05 and the GRID Requirements, under which projects bear the cost of new power infrastructure that serves them.

policyExposure.regime: Pennsylvania Executive Order 2026-05 (Responsible Infrastructure Development, 'GRID' Requirements)
policyExposure.exposure: The company invokes the order in its August 2026 release; its behind-the-meter model is the form of compliance it claims. No PJM queue entry or utility filing for Keystone Connect exists on the record, so the grid half of the 'dual utility' plan is undocumented.

policyExposure.regime: Pennsylvania air-quality permitting for on-site generation (PA DEP)
policyExposure.exposure: The company says Keystone Connect is 'currently powered by turbines' and plans a plant the Environmental Integrity Project models at 2,700 MW, yet no DEP air-quality plan approval, general permit or Title V in TECfusions' or Tecfusions Keystone LLC's name appears in the PA Bulletin through September 2026. The permits located are NPDES and water-quality permits.

The Office of Open Records ordered the company's US$250k DCED pitch unredacted; TECfusions petitioned Commonwealth Court to keep it sealed and the case is pending. The proposal 'became the target of lawsuits and partially inspired a local moratorium' (Technical.ly).

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that TECfusions signs for its own power chain, generation included, and that its buying is small today and undocumented as to vendors. Basis: the RACP scope ('generation, UPS, switchgear, cabling'), the founder's 'continuous duty-rated equipment' remark, the deck's 'domestic sourcing of Transformers, HVAC, immersion cooling', and the supply-chain blog listing transformer, switchgear, chiller, generator and UPS lead times; against that, 55 MW live across three sites, 2 MW at the flagship, and no OEM named anywhere. Indicator to watch: a DEP air-quality application or a turbine order naming an OEM for New Kensington.

(High confidence) We assess the '3 GW' and '1 GW leased' figures as marketing, and the deck's phase table as the company's real position. Basis: the company's own July 2026 deck states 2 MW live and 10 MW contracted at Keystone Connect and footnotes the 3 GW as management estimates 'subject to significant risks of change'; the TensorWave figure is restated as 'anchor tenant with right-of-first-refusal'; TensorWave's Series B names other capacity and Fermi America signed it for 222 MW. Indicator to watch: the S-4, which must carry audited financials and the contracted-MW schedule.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the SPAC as likely to close at a lower cash level than the trust implies, if it closes. Basis: US$353M in trust with a US$45M minimum cash condition and a US$35M PIPE; the CFO-designate's hope to 'retain a lot of that trust money'; no S-4 filed two months after signing; a founder risk factor on prior convictions; an outside date of 31 Mar 2027. Redemptions on 2026-vintage SPACs are the base rate this rests on, not a company fact. Indicator to watch: the S-4 filing date and the redemption figure at the shareholder vote.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the township, not the utility, is the binding constraint on Keystone Connect through 2027. Basis: the moratorium, the draft 'bring your own baseload' ordinance, the land-use appeal and the Right-to-Know case all sit at township and county level; no PJM or utility process is on the record to be delayed. Indicator to watch: the 7 Oct 2026 supervisors' meeting and the ordinance adopted before 2 Nov.

(Low confidence) We assess that batteries, SSTs and 800 VDC are outside the company's plans. Basis: the only storage mention is a generic blog on FERC Order 2222 resources; nothing on tecfusions.com mentions solid-state transformers, 800 VDC or HVDC; the deck's 'immersion cooling' and 'domestic transformers' point to conventional MV distribution. This is an inference from absence on a thin record. Indicator to watch: the equipment list in any Phase 2 land-development application.

metrics.name: Revenue
metrics.result: The webinar describes the financials as 'unaudited' with an audit 'in process'; none are on the record

metrics.name: Debt
metrics.actual: 'Over $300 million' 15-year loan for Clarksville Phase I from an unnamed 'dedicated investor'; US$160M allocated to construction (31 Oct 2024)
metrics.result: Lender, rate and security undisclosed; funding began January 2024 'in response to urgent capacity needs from a key tenant'

periods.commentary: Clarksville's first halls were built and leased in this year; the TensorWave '1 GW' commitment and the Alcoa campus purchase closed in Q4.

metrics.name: Live capacity
metrics.actual: Tucson 14.4 MW delivered in 2025 'in under four months'; Clarksville four halls (37.5 MW) leased
metrics.result: Company releases; no MW figure is audited

periods.commentary: The year of the Keystone Connect announcement, the RACP grant and the Chile land deal.

periods.period: 2026 year to date (September) and business-combination projections

metrics.name: Live and contracted capacity (Jul 2026)
metrics.actual: Clarksville 37 MW live and fully leased (42 MW under contract for Phase 2); Tucson 16 MW live plus 12 MW contracted; New Kensington 2 MW live plus 10 MW contracted
metrics.result: Business Combination Agreement release and investor deck

metrics.name: Projected revenue (deck slide 24, unaudited)
metrics.actual: US$110M (2026), US$289M (2027), US$2.14B (2028); MW in service 92, 422 and 1,467; net income –US$23M, –US$10M and US$189M
metrics.result: Management projections; capex US$1.4B, US$16.9B and US$16.1B 'assumed to be debt financed' at 'approximately 6% to 13%'; the New Kensington plant 'contributes ~$500M in 2028'

metrics.name: SPAC terms
metrics.actual: US$4.0B pre-money; 400.0M new shares at US$10.00; pro forma EV about US$4.2B; US$35M PIPE (Eleven Ventures); about US$353M in trust at 30 Jun 2026; minimum cash US$45M
metrics.result: Apex Treasury 8-K and 10-Q; no S-4 filed as of 29 Sep 2026

metrics.name: Public incentives
metrics.actual: US$2M Pennsylvania RACP grant for Keystone Connect Phase I infrastructure

periods.commentary: Every forward figure is the company's; the only externally checked numbers are the live megawatts and the trust balance. The refresh calendar carries the company as a private quarterly row until the SPAC closes, at which point it becomes a dated row.

financials.commentary: A three-year-old private company with no published financial statements, one disclosed loan from an unnamed lender, and a pending SPAC whose deck projects a twentyfold revenue rise in two years on US$34B of debt-funded capex. Read the projections as the price of the equity story, not as guidance.
